miriam: Quick experiment notes — onboarded llama-mini-7b (q4f) with our fast-lookahead decode prototype on a small canary.

miriam: TL;DR: token latency down ~22% vs baseline q4f + small quality delta. details below.

sam: nice — what config did you flip for "fast-lookahead"? any non-default flags?

miriam: enabled three things: early-lookahead window=4, speculative-hypothesis=2, kv-warmup=true
Here's the minimal run command I used:
``
./run_infer --model llama-mini-7b-q4f --decode=fast-lookahead \
  --lookahead-window=4 --spec-hyps=2 --kv-warmup=1 --batch=8
```

ada: can you paste the perf numbers (p50/p95/tokens/sec) so I can add to the dashboard?

miriam: sure
p50 per-token: 38ms (baseline q4f 49ms)
p95 per-token: 92ms (baseline 110ms)
avg tokens/sec per GPU: 120 tok/s (baseline 98 tok/s)
cpu overhead: +6% (scheduler thread spinups)

kai: interesting. how about quality — did you run the eval holdouts (instruct/e2e QA)?

miriam: ran the usual onboarding suite (instruct-acc, openqa, summarization) on 1k prompts. summary:
- instruct-acc: 92.1% (baseline q4f fp16-ish: 92.7%) -> -0.6 pts
- openqa: F1 0.72 -> 0.715 (-0.005)
- summarization ROUGE-L: 0.433 -> 0.428 (-0.005)

sam: so small regressions. are they statistically significant or noise?

miriam: borderline. CI around +-0.4% for instruct-acc, so treat as possible small degrade. dug into failures: most regressions are on long-context summarize prompts (>=1024 tokens) where lookahead occasionally picks a top-1 that changes sentence boundary.

ada: any easy mitigations? fallbacks?

miriam: yes — two quick ideas:
1) hybrid mode: enable lookahead only for first N tokens (N=32) then revert to baseline.
2) increase speculative-hyps to 3 for long-contexts (costs perf a bit).

miriam: I ran a short hybrid run: lookahead N=32 -> p50 41ms, p95 98ms, instruct-acc drop reduced to -0.2 pts. so good tradeoff.

kai: can you share one concrete failure pair (baseline vs fast-lookahead) for triage?

miriam: example (summarize prompt truncated):
baseline:
"In summary, the client needs an API rate limit of 1000 rps, retry backoff of 500ms..."
fast-lookahead:
"In summary, the client needs an API limit of 1000, increasing backoff..." -> changed phrasing, lost 'rps' detail leading to lower QA score.

sam: ok. sounds like lookahead sometimes prefers shorter phrasing. is there any temperature/artifact confound? same sampling seed?

miriam: deterministic sampling seed=42 for these runs. we also tried temp=0.7 vs 0.2 — higher temp increased variance and regressions; keep temp at 0.2 for canary.

ada: do we have cost delta estimate for Dedicated-hosted units if we flip this to prod? lower tokens/sec per GPU means less cost, but speculative hyps adds compute.

miriam: rough unit economics: for typical web-chat workload (avg seq len 128), hybrid N=32 gives ~12% token-cost reduction; full lookahead gives ~18% reduction but with slightly higher CPU overhead and small quality risk.

deploy-bot: deploy-started: canary/fast-lookahead/3-nodes @ 1717000100

kai: plan proposal: 1) keep canary running on 3 nodes for 24h, 2) run full 10k prompt A/B with hybrid N=32, 3) if instruct-acc delta <= 0.3 pts rollback else iterate.

sam: +1. also add a prompt-tag to detect long-contexts and route them to non-lookahead fallback automatically.

miriam: added a telemetry flag in the run: lookahead_diagnostics=true — will post logs to /tmp/llm-lookahead-logs.tar

ada: great, please add the small experiment summary to the onboarding board and tag @eng-sre for CPU overhead watch.

miriam: will do. saving raw outputs & diffs to s3://onboard-outputs/llama-mini-7b/fastlook-1717000000.tar.gz

miriam: will post a short follow-up once the 24h canary finishes.

sam: thanks — appreciate the quick bench.

deploy-bot: deploy-complete: canary/fast-lookahead/3-nodes @ 1717000150

miriam: (note) next iteration: try lookahead-window=6 + hybrid N=16 as a middle ground.

ada: tagging this thread into the onboarding tracker.

miriam: :thumbsup:
